N01.title: Forward Head Posture (Tech Neck)
N01.message:
Forward head posture develops when the head gradually shifts ahead of the shoulders, often from long hours looking at phones or screens, placing extra strain on the neck's muscles and joints. You may commonly experience:
- A persistent ache at the base of the neck that builds through the day.
- Tightness across the shoulders and upper back.
- A feeling of heaviness in the head, especially by evening.
- Reduced range of motion when turning or tilting the head.
- Headaches that seem to start from the neck.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help correct this posture over time.**

N02.title: Cervical Spondylosis
N02.message:
Cervical spondylosis is a gradual, age-related change in the discs and joints of the neck that can lead to stiffness and discomfort, particularly noticeable first thing in the morning. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that is worse on waking and eases slightly through the day.
- A grating or clicking sensation with neck movement.
- Reduced flexibility when looking side to side.
- Occasional discomfort that spreads toward the shoulder.
- Sensitivity to sudden or jerky neck movements.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help manage stiffness and maintain mobility.**

N05.title: Cervical Radiculopathy (Pinched Nerve)
N05.message:
Cervical radiculopathy happens when a nerve in the neck becomes compressed or irritated, which can cause sensations that travel beyond the neck itself. You may commonly experience:
- Sharp or tingling sensations that radiate into the shoulder or arm.
- Numbness or a "pins and needles" feeling in the hand or fingers.
- Weakness when gripping or lifting with the affected arm.
- Discomfort that worsens with certain neck positions.
- Symptoms that ease when the neck is supported and well-aligned.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine — this is one where following the guided approach closely really matters.**

N03.title: Neck Strain
N03.message:
Neck strain is a common, usually short-term irritation of the muscles or soft tissue in the neck, often from an awkward sleeping position or sudden movement. You may commonly experience:
- Soreness that's more noticeable when turning the head.
- Tenderness to the touch along one side of the neck.
- A general feeling of tightness rather than sharp pain.
- Discomfort that improves gradually over a few days.
- Mild stiffness first thing in the morning.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support a smooth recovery.**

N04.title: Tension Headache
N04.message:
Tension headaches are often linked to tightness in the neck and shoulder muscles, especially from stress or long periods in one posture. You may commonly experience:
- A dull, band-like pressure around the head.
- Tightness at the base of the skull that seems to trigger the headache.
- Discomfort that builds gradually rather than appearing suddenly.
- Headaches that are more frequent during high-stress or high-screen-time periods.
- Some relief when the neck and shoulders are stretched or relaxed.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help ease this tension at its source.**

N06.title: Postural Neck Fatigue (Desk Work) / Cervical Disc Bulge (Degenerative Disc)
N06.message:
This combines general fatigue from long static neck postures with early-stage disc changes that can add localized stiffness or mild discomfort that sometimes spreads. You may commonly experience:
- A tired, heavy feeling in the neck by the end of the workday.
- Stiffness that builds gradually rather than appearing suddenly.
- Occasional mild discomfort that extends slightly beyond the neck itself.
- Reduced comfort holding one position (like screen work) for long periods.
- Relief when changing position or taking movement breaks.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine, kept gentle and controlled given the disc involvement.**

N07.title: Trapezius Muscle Spasm
N07.message:
A trapezius spasm is a sudden tightening of the muscle running from the neck to the shoulder, often linked to stress or holding the shoulders raised for long periods. You may commonly experience:
- A tight, knotted feeling across the top of the shoulder.
- Discomfort that can radiate up toward the base of the skull.
- Increased tightness during periods of stress.
- Reduced ease of movement when shrugging or rotating the shoulder.
- Some relief with warmth or gentle movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help release this tension.**

S01.title: Rotator Cuff Strain
S01.message:
A rotator cuff strain involves the group of muscles and tendons that stabilize the shoulder joint, often affected by overuse or repetitive overhead movement. You may commonly experience:
- Pain when lifting the arm, especially overhead.
- A dull ache that can worsen at night.
- Weakness when reaching or lifting.
- Discomfort with certain rotating movements of the arm.
- Reduced comfort sleeping on the affected side.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support safe, gradual recovery.**

S02.title: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis)
S02.message:
Frozen shoulder is a progressive stiffening of the shoulder joint's capsule that develops gradually and can significantly limit movement. You may commonly experience:
- A steadily worsening restriction in shoulder movement.
- Pain that can be more noticeable at night.
- Difficulty with everyday movements like reaching behind your back.
- Stiffness that may improve very slowly over an extended period.
- Discomfort with sudden or forced movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine — gentle consistency matters more than intensity here.**

S03.title: Shoulder Impingement Syndrome
S03.message:
Shoulder impingement occurs when tendons in the shoulder get compressed during certain arm movements, most often overhead reaching. You may commonly experience:
- Pain specifically when raising the arm to shoulder height or above.
- A pinching sensation with certain movements.
- Weakness during overhead activity.
- Discomfort that eases when the arm is lowered.
- Increased sensitivity with repeated overhead motion.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help correct the underlying movement pattern.**

S04.title: Rounded Shoulder Posture
S04.message:
Rounded shoulders develop when the chest muscles shorten and the upper back muscles lengthen and weaken, often from long periods of sitting. You may commonly experience:
- Shoulders that visibly curve forward when relaxed.
- Tightness across the chest.
- Fatigue in the upper back from holding the corrected posture.
- A tendency to slouch that feels hard to consciously correct.
- Mild discomfort between the shoulder blades.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help rebalance this posture over time.**

S05.title: Shoulder Pain from Side-Sleeping
S05.message:
This type of shoulder discomfort develops from direct, unsupported pressure on the shoulder joint during side-sleeping over time. You may commonly experience:
- Soreness that's most noticeable first thing in the morning.
- Discomfort specifically on the side you tend to sleep on.
- A dull ache that eases as you move around during the day.
- Reduced comfort lying directly on that shoulder.
- Occasional stiffness when reaching overhead after waking.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help relieve this pressure-related discomfort.**

S06.title: Bursitis of the Shoulder
S06.message:
Bursitis is inflammation of the small fluid-filled cushion that protects the shoulder joint, which can make movement and pressure uncomfortable. You may commonly experience:
- Tenderness with direct pressure on the shoulder.
- Pain that increases with movement, especially overhead.
- Mild swelling or warmth around the joint.
- Discomfort that can interfere with sleeping on that side.
- Stiffness following periods of rest.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support gentle, gradual movement recovery.**

S09.title: AC Joint Strain
S09.message:
The AC joint connects the collarbone to the shoulder blade, and strain here often follows repetitive load or a minor knock. You may commonly experience:
- A specific point of tenderness at the top of the shoulder.
- Discomfort when carrying weight on that side.
- Pain with movements that cross the arm over the body.
- Mild swelling directly over the joint.
- Sensitivity to direct pressure in that area.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support recovery of this joint.**

S11.title: Shoulder Tightness from Stress
S11.message:
Stress-related shoulder tightness develops when shoulders are unconsciously held raised or tense over extended periods. You may commonly experience:
- A persistent, tight feeling across the top of the shoulders.
- Tension that seems to build during stressful periods.
- Difficulty consciously relaxing the shoulders.
- Mild discomfort that can extend toward the neck.
- Relief that comes with deliberate relaxation or movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help release this tension.**

S12.title: Referred Shoulder Pain from Neck Issues
S12.message:
Sometimes shoulder discomfort actually originates from the neck, with pain or sensation "referred" down into the shoulder area. You may commonly experience:
- Shoulder discomfort that doesn't clearly link to shoulder movement itself.
- Some relief or change in symptoms when the neck position changes.
- Pain that may accompany neck stiffness or reduced neck mobility.
- A sensation that feels deeper than a typical muscular ache.
- Symptoms that don't fully resolve with shoulder-focused rest alone.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below — addressing the neck alongside the shoulder is often key here.**

U01.title: Thoracic Kyphosis (Slouched Upper Back)
U01.message:
This describes a gradual forward curving of the upper back, most often linked to long periods of sitting and screen use. You may commonly experience:
- A visibly rounded upper back posture.
- Fatigue between the shoulder blades by the end of the day.
- Difficulty maintaining an upright posture for long periods.
- Mild stiffness when trying to stand fully tall.
- Tightness across the chest that pulls the shoulders forward.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help correct this curve over time.**

U02.title: Upper Back Muscle Fatigue (Desk Work)
U02.message:
This is general fatigue in the upper back's muscles from holding a static position through long work hours. You may commonly experience:
- A tired, heavy feeling between the shoulder blades.
- Discomfort that builds progressively through the day.
- Some relief with movement or stretching breaks.
- Stiffness that's more noticeable after sitting for extended periods.
- A tendency to slouch as the muscles tire.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build resilience in this area.**

U03.title: Rhomboid Strain
U03.message:
The rhomboids are the muscles between your shoulder blades, and strain here often comes from repetitive poor posture or overuse. You may commonly experience:
- A localized ache between the shoulder blades.
- Discomfort that increases with prolonged slouching.
- Tenderness when the area is pressed.
- Mild stiffness when pulling the shoulder blades together.
- Some relief with gentle movement and posture correction.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support this area's recovery.**

U04.title: Postural Upper Back Pain (Screen Use)
U04.message:
Extended forward-leaning toward screens places ongoing strain on the muscles supporting the upper back. You may commonly experience:
- Discomfort that correlates closely with screen time.
- A tired ache across the upper back by evening.
- Tightness that eases somewhat with posture correction.
- Mild stiffness when sitting upright after slouching.
- A tendency to lean forward without noticing.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build better postural habits.**

U06.title: Upper Back Pain from Sagging Mattress
U06.message:
When a mattress no longer provides even support, the upper back can curve unnaturally through the night, leading to strain. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's most noticeable first thing in the morning.
- Discomfort that improves somewhat as you move through the day.
- A sense that your sleep surface isn't adequately supportive.
- Mild aching along the upper spine after waking.
- Symptoms that seem tied specifically to how you slept.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support your upper back alongside proper mattress support.**

U07.title: Costovertebral Joint Discomfort
U07.message:
This involves discomfort at the small joints where the ribs meet the spine, often aggravated by poor posture or twisting. You may commonly experience:
- A localized ache along the upper back, sometimes wrapping toward the ribs.
- Discomfort that increases with certain twisting movements.
- Mild sensitivity with deep breathing in some cases.
- Stiffness after prolonged sitting.
- Some relief with gentle upper back mobility work.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support this area gently.**

U09.title: Scapular Stabilizer Weakness
U09.message:
This refers to weakness in the muscles that keep the shoulder blade properly positioned, which affects overall upper back posture. You may commonly experience:
- Shoulder blades that sit or move asymmetrically.
- Fatigue in the upper back with sustained postures.
- Some difficulty maintaining an upright, "shoulders back" posture.
- Mild discomfort with overhead or reaching movements.
- A tendency toward rounded shoulder posture.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build strength in this area.**

U11.title: Postural Strain from Driving
U11.message:
Long periods of driving in a fixed position, especially with limited back support, can strain the upper back over time. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that builds during and after long drives.
- Discomfort that's specific to your driving posture.
- A tired, tight feeling across the upper back afterward.
- Some relief with stretching after a drive.
- Sensitivity to seat support quality.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help counteract this strain.**

U12.title: Mid-Back Stiffness (Prolonged Sitting)
U12.message:
Extended sitting without movement reduces mobility in the mid-back over time, leading to a stiff, tight feeling. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's most noticeable after sitting for a long stretch.
- Some relief with movement or standing breaks.
- A tight, restricted feeling when trying to twist or rotate the torso.
- Discomfort that eases gradually once you start moving.
- Reduced ease of movement compared to earlier in the day.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help restore mobility here.**

L01.title: Lumbar Strain (General Lower Back Pain)
L01.message:
Lumbar strain typically involves micro-tears in the muscles or ligaments of the lower back, often caused by overuse or sudden movements. You may commonly experience:
- A dull, aching pain in the lower back that worsens with movement.
- Stiffness and difficulty standing up straight.
- Muscle spasms that can feel sharp or restrictive.
- Discomfort that increases after prolonged sitting or bending.
- Trouble finding a comfortable position to sleep.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized stretching and strengthening routine to aid your recovery.**

L02.title: Sciatica
L02.message:
Sciatica occurs when the sciatic nerve, running from the lower back down the leg, becomes irritated or compressed. You may commonly experience:
- Pain that radiates from the lower back into the leg.
- Numbness or tingling that follows a similar path.
- Discomfort that worsens with prolonged sitting.
- Some weakness in the affected leg.
- Symptoms that shift with certain positions or movements.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine — following it carefully matters given the nerve involvement.**

L03.title: Herniated/Bulging Disc (Lumbar)
L03.message:
This involves a disc in the lower back bulging or herniating, which can sometimes press on nearby nerves. You may commonly experience:
- Localized lower back pain that may extend further.
- Discomfort that worsens with bending or lifting.
- Stiffness when transitioning between positions.
- Occasional tingling or altered sensation in the leg.
- Symptoms that ease with certain supported positions.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine, designed to be gentle and progressive.**

L04.title: Poor Mattress Support-Related Pain
L04.message:
When a mattress no longer supports the lower back's natural curve, the hips can sink out of alignment through the night. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness and aching that's most noticeable on waking.
- Discomfort that improves somewhat once you're up and moving.
- A sense that your current sleep surface isn't holding you well.
- Recurring morning soreness night after night.
- Symptoms directly tied to how and where you slept.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support your back alongside proper mattress support.**

L05.title: Lower Back Pain from Prolonged Sitting
L05.message:
Extended sitting compresses the lower back's discs and reduces blood flow to supporting muscles over time. You may commonly experience:
- Discomfort that builds the longer you sit.
- Some relief when standing or moving around.
- Stiffness when first standing up after sitting.
- A tired, achy feeling by the end of a seated day.
- Reduced comfort maintaining an upright seated posture.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help counteract prolonged sitting.**

L06.title: Sacroiliac (SI) Joint Dysfunction
L06.message:
This involves irritation of the joint connecting the spine to the pelvis, often causing pain that's more noticeable on one side. You may commonly experience:
- One-sided lower back or pelvic discomfort.
- Pain that can increase with certain movements like standing from sitting.
- A feeling of instability in the pelvis or lower back.
- Discomfort with uneven weight-bearing activities.
- Symptoms that may shift depending on posture.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help support this joint.**

L07.title: Lumbar Spondylosis
L07.message:
Lumbar spondylosis refers to age-related wear of the lower spine's joints and discs, often causing stiffness especially in the morning. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's most pronounced first thing in the morning.
- Gradual easing of stiffness as the day progresses.
- Mild discomfort with certain movements or positions.
- Reduced flexibility compared to previous years.
- Sensitivity to sudden or heavy movements.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help maintain mobility.**

L08.title: Postural Lower Back Pain (Standing/Retail Work)
L08.message:
Prolonged standing, common in retail and service roles, fatigues the lower back's supporting muscles over time. You may commonly experience:
- An aching lower back that builds through a standing shift.
- Some relief when sitting or shifting weight between legs.
- Fatigue that accumulates over consecutive standing days.
- Discomfort that's more noticeable by the end of the day.
- A tendency to favor one leg while standing.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build standing endurance.**

L09.title: Lower Back Stiffness from Stomach Sleeping
L09.message:
Stomach sleeping can arch the lower back unnaturally, placing strain on it across a full night's rest. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's most noticeable on waking.
- Discomfort that improves somewhat once you begin moving.
- A recurring pattern tied specifically to your sleep position.
- Mild lower back tightness that eases through the morning.
- Some difficulty finding a comfortable sleeping position.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help ease this stiffness.**

L10.title: Muscle Imbalance-Related Pain (Weak Core)
L10.message:
When the core muscles are underdeveloped, the lower back takes on more support than it's built for during daily activity. You may commonly experience:
- General lower back fatigue during everyday movement.
- Discomfort that increases with activities requiring stability.
- A sense of reduced "support" through the midsection.
- Mild soreness after standing or activity-heavy days.
- Symptoms that may improve as core strength builds.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build supportive core strength.**

L11.title: Lower Back Pain from Heavy Lifting
L11.message:
Improper lifting form places excessive, concentrated strain on the lower back's muscles and discs. You may commonly experience:
- Sudden or building discomfort following a lift.
- Stiffness that makes bending or straightening uncomfortable.
- Muscle tightness or spasm in the lower back.
- Discomfort that's sensitive to further lifting or bending.
- Some improvement with rest and gentle movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support safe recovery.**

L12.title: Degenerative Disc Discomfort - Lower Back
L12.message:
This reflects gradual wear of the lumbar discs over time, causing intermittent stiffness and reduced flexibility. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that comes and goes rather than staying constant.
- Reduced flexibility compared to previous years.
- Mild discomfort with prolonged inactivity or high-impact movement.
- Symptoms that respond well to gentle, consistent movement.
- Occasional flare-ups following unusual strain.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help manage this over time.**

L13.title: Pregnancy-Related Lower Back Strain
L13.message:
Postural and weight-distribution changes during pregnancy commonly place extra strain on the lower back. You may commonly experience:
- A dull ache that builds as pregnancy progresses.
- Discomfort that's more noticeable with prolonged standing or walking.
- Some difficulty finding a comfortable sleeping position.
- Mild stiffness when changing positions.
- Symptoms that shift as your body adapts.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, doctor-approved routine tailored to this stage.**

K01.title: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome (Runner's Knee)
K01.message:
This involves pain around or behind the kneecap, often linked to overuse or how the kneecap tracks during movement. You may commonly experience:
- An ache around or behind the kneecap.
- Discomfort that increases with stairs, squatting, or prolonged sitting.
- A grinding or clicking sensation with knee movement.
- Mild swelling after activity.
- Symptoms that build gradually rather than appearing suddenly.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support proper kneecap tracking.**

K02.title: Osteoarthritis of the Knee
K02.message:
Knee osteoarthritis is age-related wear of the joint's cartilage, causing stiffness and discomfort especially with activity. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's more noticeable after rest or first thing in the morning.
- Discomfort that increases with activity or weight-bearing.
- A grating sensation during movement.
- Mild swelling around the joint at times.
- Reduced flexibility compared to previous years.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help maintain mobility and strength.**

K03.title: Meniscus Tear
K03.message:
The meniscus is cartilage that cushions the knee joint, and tears here often follow a twisting movement. You may commonly experience:
- A sharp or catching sensation with certain movements.
- Swelling that develops following the initial injury.
- Difficulty fully straightening the knee.
- A sense of the knee "locking" or "giving way" at times.
- Discomfort along the joint line.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support safe recovery.**

K04.title: ACL (Anterior Cruciate Ligament) Sprain/Tear
K04.message:
The ACL is a key stabilizing ligament in the knee, commonly affected by sudden stops or direction changes. You may commonly experience:
- A feeling of instability or the knee "giving way."
- Swelling that develops relatively quickly after injury.
- Discomfort with pivoting or sudden direction changes.
- Reduced confidence in the knee's stability.
- Stiffness following the initial injury period.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, carefully progressed recovery routine.**

K05.title: MCL (Medial Collateral Ligament) Sprain
K05.message:
The MCL supports the inner side of the knee, and strain here often follows a sideways impact or stress. You may commonly experience:
- Tenderness along the inner side of the knee.
- Discomfort with side-to-side movement.
- Mild swelling near the inner knee.
- A sense of instability with certain movements.
- Symptoms that ease with supported, controlled movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support recovery.**

K06.title: Patellar Tendinitis (Jumper's Knee)
K06.message:
This is inflammation of the tendon connecting the kneecap to the shinbone, common with jumping-heavy activity. You may commonly experience:
- Tenderness just below the kneecap.
- Discomfort that increases with jumping, running, or stairs.
- Stiffness after periods of rest following activity.
- Mild swelling in the area at times.
- Symptoms that build gradually with repeated activity.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support this tendon's recovery.**

K07.title: IT Band Syndrome (Iliotibial Band Syndrome)
K07.message:
This involves tightness or friction of the band running along the outer thigh to the knee, causing pain on the outer side of the joint. You may commonly experience:
- A sharp or aching pain on the outer knee.
- Discomfort that tends to build during repetitive activity like running.
- Tightness along the outer thigh.
- Symptoms that ease with rest but return with activity.
- Sensitivity to downhill movement or repeated bending.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help release this tightness.**

K08.title: Bursitis of the Knee
K08.message:
Knee bursitis is inflammation of the small fluid-filled sac that cushions the joint, making certain movements and pressure uncomfortable. You may commonly experience:
- Tenderness with direct pressure on the knee.
- Mild swelling or warmth around the joint.
- Discomfort with kneeling or bending.
- Stiffness following rest.
- Symptoms that can fluctuate with activity level.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support gentle recovery.**

K09.title: Chondromalacia Patella
K09.message:
This involves softening or breakdown of the cartilage under the kneecap, often causing a grinding or aching sensation. You may commonly experience:
- A dull ache around the front of the knee.
- A grinding sensation with certain movements.
- Discomfort with stairs or prolonged sitting.
- Mild swelling at times.
- Symptoms that build gradually.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support the joint.**

K10.title: PCL (Posterior Cruciate Ligament) Sprain
K10.message:
The PCL stabilizes backward movement of the knee, often affected by a direct blow to the front of the knee. You may commonly experience:
- Mild to moderate swelling following the injury.
- A sense of instability, particularly with certain movements.
- Discomfort at the back of the knee.
- Stiffness in the days following injury.
- Reduced confidence with weight-bearing activity initially.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, carefully progressed routine.**

K11.title: Knee Pain from Weak Quadriceps
K11.message:
When the quadriceps muscles are underdeveloped, the knee joint has less support during everyday movement, leading to strain and instability. You may commonly experience:
- A general ache around the knee during activity.
- A sense that the knee feels less stable than it should.
- Fatigue in the thigh during stairs or prolonged standing.
- Discomfort that may ease as strength builds.
- Mild soreness after activity-heavy days.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build supportive strength.**

K12.title: Patellar Dislocation/Subluxation
K12.message:
This occurs when the kneecap partially or fully shifts out of its normal groove. You may commonly experience:
- A visible or felt shift in the kneecap's position.
- Sudden pain at the time of the shift.
- Swelling that develops afterward.
- A sense of apprehension or instability with certain movements.
- Reduced confidence in the knee following the episode.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, carefully guided recovery routine.**

K13.title: Gout in the Knee
K13.message:
Gout is a buildup of uric acid crystals in the joint, causing sudden, sharp pain and swelling. You may commonly experience:
- Sudden, intense pain, often without clear cause.
- Noticeable swelling and warmth around the joint.
- Sensitivity to even light touch or pressure.
- Discomfort that can flare unpredictably.
- Reduced mobility during a flare.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine, to be used once a flare has settled.**

K14.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis of the Knee
K14.message:
This is an autoimmune condition causing inflammation, stiffness, and swelling in the knee joint. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's often worse in the morning.
- Swelling and warmth around the joint.
- Discomfort that can vary with disease activity.
- Fatigue alongside the joint symptoms.
- Symptoms that may affect both knees.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, gentle mobility routine.**

K15.title: Referred Knee Pain from Hip Issues
K15.message:
Sometimes knee discomfort actually originates from the hip, due to shared nerve pathways between the two joints. You may commonly experience:
- Knee discomfort that doesn't clearly connect to knee movement itself.
- Some change in symptoms when hip position or movement changes.
- Pain that may accompany hip stiffness or reduced hip mobility.
- Symptoms that don't fully resolve with knee-focused rest alone.
- A sensation that feels different from a typical joint ache.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below — addressing the hip alongside the knee is often key here.**

K16.title: Knee Pain from Poor Footwear/Overpronation
K16.message:
Improper foot alignment can place uneven, ongoing stress on the knee joint over time. You may commonly experience:
- Knee discomfort that seems tied to specific footwear or activities.
- Uneven wear patterns you may notice on your shoes.
- Mild discomfort that builds with walking or standing.
- A sense of the knee "rolling" inward during movement.
- Symptoms that improve with supportive footwear.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support better alignment.**

K17.title: Postural Knee Strain from Prolonged Standing
K17.message:
Common in retail and service roles, prolonged standing fatigues the muscles supporting the knee joint over time. You may commonly experience:
- An ache around the knee that builds during a standing shift.
- Some relief when sitting or shifting position.
- Fatigue that accumulates over consecutive standing days.
- Discomfort that's more noticeable by the end of the day.
- A tendency to lock or lean on one leg while standing.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help build standing endurance.**

K18.title: Knee Stiffness from Prolonged Sitting
K18.message:
Extended sedentary periods reduce knee mobility over time, leading to a stiff, restricted feeling. You may commonly experience:
- Stiffness that's most noticeable after sitting for a long stretch.
- Some relief with movement or standing breaks.
- A restricted feeling when first bending the knee after sitting.
- Discomfort that eases gradually once you start moving.
- Reduced ease of movement compared to earlier in the day.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help restore mobility.**

C01.title: Calf Muscle Strain
C01.message:
A calf strain involves a stretch or minor tear in the calf muscle, often from sudden exertion. You may commonly experience:
- A sudden, sharp discomfort during activity.
- Tenderness along the calf when touched.
- Tightness that limits full ankle movement.
- Mild swelling or bruising in some cases.
- Discomfort that increases with pushing off the foot.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized recovery routine.**

C02.title: Calf Muscle Tightness
C02.message:
General calf tightness often builds from limited stretching, prolonged sitting, or repetitive activity. You may commonly experience:
- A persistent, tight feeling in the lower leg.
- Reduced flexibility when flexing the foot upward.
- Mild discomfort that increases with activity.
- A sense of restriction rather than sharp pain.
- Some relief with stretching or gentle movement.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized stretching routine.**

C03.title: Calf Cramps
C03.message:
Calf cramps are sudden, involuntary muscle contractions that can be sharp and momentarily intense. You may commonly experience:
- Sudden, sharp tightening of the calf muscle.
- Discomfort that often occurs at night or after activity.
- Temporary hardness or visible tightening of the muscle.
- Residual soreness after the cramp passes.
- Occasional recurrence during sleep.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to help reduce cramp frequency.**

C04.title: Shin-to-Calf Muscle Pain
C04.message:
This describes discomfort spanning the shin and calf, often linked to overuse or muscular imbalance in the lower leg. You may commonly experience:
- An ache that spans from the shin toward the calf.
- Discomfort that increases with walking or running.
- Tightness that builds with repetitive activity.
- Mild tenderness along the shin.
- Symptoms that ease with rest.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support this area.**

C05.title: Ankle Sprain
C05.message:
An ankle sprain is a stretch or tear of the ligaments supporting the ankle, usually from an awkward twist or roll. You may commonly experience:
- Swelling around the ankle joint.
- Discomfort or instability when bearing weight.
- Bruising that may develop over the following days.
- Reduced range of motion in the joint.
- A sense of the ankle feeling "weak" during recovery.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, carefully progressed recovery routine.**

C06.title: Achilles Tendinopathy
C06.message:
This involves irritation or degeneration of the Achilles tendon, often from repetitive strain. You may commonly experience:
- Discomfort just above the heel, especially with activity.
- Stiffness that's more noticeable first thing in the morning.
- Tenderness along the back of the lower leg.
- Symptoms that build gradually with repeated activity.
- Some relief with rest, returning with renewed activity.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized, gradual loading routine.**

C07.title: High Arch / Low Arch of Foot
C07.message:
Variations in foot arch height affect how weight is distributed through the foot and can contribute to discomfort elsewhere in the leg. You may commonly experience:
- Uneven wear patterns on footwear.
- Discomfort that builds with prolonged standing or walking.
- A tendency toward related knee, ankle, or lower back strain.
- Fatigue in the feet by the end of the day.
- Symptoms that improve with appropriate footwear or support.
- **Please refer to the Exercises section below for your personalized routine to support better foot alignment.**
